description: Trigger evals for repo-consistency-sweep: it fires when at least one slice is implemented and the code should be checked against known bug classes before packaging, while review-hard, apply-sweep-triage, security-review and pr-package handle design-level risk review, saving triage choices, a security pass, and PR delivery.

should_trigger: Slice 2 is coded. Before I open the PR, scan the changed files for convention drift, ordering bugs and missing tenant checks.
run a pre-PR pass over my diff for the usual defect classes
I want the boring half of code review handled automatically: type-safety gaps, missing awaits, unscoped queries in the orders service. Check the branch and skip anything I already declined last time.
Two slices are done in the invoicing task. Compare the new handlers against our bug-class library and give me a findings snapshot I can triage.
Can you look for the same kinds of defects our reviewers keep flagging (log injection, unhandled promise rejections, hardcoded timeouts) across the files this task touched?

should_not_trigger.prompt: The slice is done. I want a real engineering review of whether the design holds up and what could break in production, not a pattern scan.
I edited the triage values in the findings file, 5 apply and 3 decline. Save them so they are remembered.
This task adds a login endpoint with JWT refresh. Do a threat model and an ASVS pass on the changes.
Nothing is coded yet. Here is the endpoint list for the refunds service; check the paths, error codes and pagination for consistency with our existing handlers before anyone writes them.
Everything is reviewed and stable. Write the PR title, body and reviewer notes from the diff against main.
